stories.title: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say
stories.summary: Spanish prosecutors say 23 sexual assaults, including nine against children, have been recorded in Ceuta since the mass influx of migrants into the Spanish exclave at the end of July. That number meant there was almost one case every day, Ceuta's chief prosecutor. Silvia Rojas said. She told El País newspaper migrant girls were "particularly vulnerable because of their irregular status in the territory". At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July and although most have returned, as many as 5,000 remain - leading to unrest in the autonomous city in North Africa and a crisis for Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. There have been scenes of violence in recent days as tensions flare up between migrants and local residents. Sánchez called the second meeting of his national security in a week on Tuesday to tackle the issue. Between 1,400 and 1,600 of the estimated 5,000 migrants still in Ceuta are children, according to Rojas. Among the suspected attackers are four Moroccans, three Spaniards and a Belgian, Efe news agency reports. Rojas said many victims did not file a report, either out of fear of because of their "current situation in Ceuta". The Spanish Society of Epidemiology has warned that violence against women "cannot be considered an isolated event". Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo said a multi-million euro aid package had been approved by the cabinet that would help provide essential services and cover care for unaccompanied children.

stories.title: Woman killed in Times Square stabbing, suspect shot dead by police
stories.summary: A 32-year-old woman was killed and another victim is in hospital following a stabbing in Times Square, New York City late on Wednesday afternoon. The suspect, a woman wielding two knifes, was shot by police. All three people were taken to hospital, where the female victim and the suspect were later pronounced dead, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a news conference. Mamdani said the second victim is in a "stable condition". He also thanked NYPD officers for preventing a "horrific attack from becoming even worse". New York Police Department (NYPD) Commissioner Jessica Tisch called the attack "an unprovoked double stabbing" that took place within approximately 20 seconds of each other. Citing preliminary information, Tisch said the NYPD call centre received several 911 calls at approximately 16:24 local time (21:00 BST) reporting a woman armed with two knives was stabbing people along Seventh Avenue in Times Square. Police believe the incident began near West 41st Street and Seventh Ave. The suspect approached a man who had just exited the subway and was standing with his wife waiting to cross the street, Tisch told a news conference. "A witness at the scene told investigators that he observed the subject remove two knives from a red Target bag before approaching the first victim. "The subject waved the knives before stabbing a 68-year-old man in the right side of his abdomen, in what appears to be a random and unprovoked attack." The 68-year-old was taken to Bellevue Hospital and is now stable.

stories.title: Live: UK PM Andy Burnham faces MPs for first time since taking office
stories.summary: The United Kingdom's new Prime Minister Andy Burnham will face lawmakers in the House of Commons on Tuesday for the first time since taking office six weeks ago. Burnham has promised to deliver renewed national optimism after the downbeat two-year tenure of predecessor Keir Starmer, who announced Tuesday that he would resign his seat in Parliament after 11 years.Watch his speech live on FRANCE 24 at 15:30pm (GMT+2).

stories.title: Ukraine moves to curtail non-defense spending — PM
stories.summary: Sergey Koretsky said the government is introducing a strict austerity regime
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.
The Ukrainian government has introduced strict austerity measures for non-military spending, Prime Minister Sergey Koretsky stated.
"The government is introducing a strict austerity regime for budget funds not allocated to defense needs," he said on the Ukrainian TV channel Rada.
Earlier, Olga Vasilevskaya-Smaglyuk, an MP from the ruling Servant of the People party, reported that Ukraine faces a financial shortfall of €49.5 billion.
Of this amount, approximately €26 billion was expected in external funding, but it's now become clear this money won't come.
For several years, Ukraine has run huge deficits.
Kiev acknowledges that the country has completely exhausted its own resources and that money is becoming hard to come by.
On August 20, Zelensky admitted that the lack of funds had become a major challenge, noting that the defense budget alone is $27 billion over.
As former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmitry Kuleba noted, no one in Kiev knows how to stop the budget-bleeding.

stories.title: SCO leaders highlight UN potential, reject 'law of jungle'
stories.summary: TASS has compiled key statements from SCO leaders
article_sentences: BISHKEK, September 1.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said the potential of the United Nations (UN) remains untapped and called for improving its effectiveness at the SCO Plus meeting.
Chinese President Xi Jinping said the world must reject the "law of the jungle" and double standards.
He called on Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) member states to work together to bring credibility back to the UN.
TASS has compiled key statements from SCO leaders.
Putin said Russia is not fully satisfied the UN, but that is nothing new: "We do not always like or are satisfied with everything the UN does.
At the same time, I must note that, to be honest, this has always been the case, practically since its creation."

The Russian president said the UN's potential remains "untapped" and called for efforts to improve the organization's effectiveness: "It is important to make efforts to improve the effectiveness of its work.
Its bodies, including the Security Council, should have broader representation from countries of the Global South and East.
Overall, the organization should adapt to the changing realities and fundamental shifts emerging in global politics and the economy."
Putin stressed that the process of building a fair multipolar world order is irreversible: "This process is objective and, frankly, irreversible, a fact that is already clear to everyone."

The Russian leader said the UN should retain its role as the main mechanism for balancing the interests of different countries: "The world organization should undoubtedly retain its role as the main mechanism for coordinating interests.
